subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity expansion & term amendment — OmniHealth
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@omnihealth.com>, Sofia Martins <sofia.martins@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity expansion & term amendment — OmniHealth

Hi Liam / Sofia,

Thanks again for the time earlier this week. As we approach the March 31 renewal window, I wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table for the Dedicated capacity expansion you requested in our renewal conversation. Summary below — full SOW and pricing attached.

What we're proposing (high level)
- Add two regional reserved pools: EU (Frankfurt) and APAC (Tokyo)
- Each pool: 24 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (configurable as 12x double-node or 24x single-node)
- Throughput guarantee: 2,000 TPS aggregate per pool (tokens/sec target under steady-state inference) with target p95 latency < 120ms for short-form generate workloads (<= 512 tokens)
- Cross-region failover: automatic policy-based routing with warm-standby KV cache and prefix prewarming; failover RTO target 90s for session continuity
- Term amendment: move from 12-month to 24-month committed term for discounted pricing and to lock capacity reservations

Attachments: SOW_omnihealth_dedicated_expansion_v1.pdf, pricing_sheet_q1_2026.xlsx

Requested next steps
1) Quick technical sync with your platform/infra team this week to confirm peering and egress constraints (30–45m). Monica and Karthik from our side will join.
2) Legal intake: we can ship a draft amendment (DocuSign) once SOW + pricing are aligned. Priya (legal) will be on the thread for redlines.
3) Target go-live window: provision pools in staging in the first week of April, production cutover mid-April — tentative and dependent on peering windows.

Can you share: a) any data residency constraints for EU pool, and b) a preferred date/time for the technical sync?

Thanks — looking forward to keeping this simple and predictable for the team.

— Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Redwood Inference — Production-grade inference made predictable
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@omnihealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Martins <sofia.martins@omnihealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 12:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated capacity expansion & term amendment — OmniHealth

Aditya — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications before we kick off with legal/infra: 

1) Latency expectations: you note p95 < 120ms for <=512 tokens. Is that measured from a browser client in Frankfurt/Tokyo, or from our backend over a private VPC peering? We need to be explicit for SLOs.
2) Failover behavior: if EU pool gets saturated or has an outage, will production traffic automatically route to US pool (we expect the short TTL DNS + routing change may add latency) or do we need to implement app-level retry logic?
3) Commitment change: 24 months is a big lift for procurement. Can we see alternative pricing for 12 months + higher monthly commit (step-up)?

We can do a tech sync Monday 23rd at 09:00 CET (works for Sofia + infra). Also, check: data residency — any PII stored in EU pool stays in EU; we require that for some datasets.

Thanks — Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering, OmniHealth
liam.oconnor@omnihealth.com | +353 1 555 9876
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@omnihealth.com>, Sofia Martins <sofia.martins@omnihealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 08:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated capacity expansion & term amendment — OmniHealth

Hi Liam / Sofia — Karthik here (Solutions). Quick answers to your bullets ahead of the sync Monday: 

- Latency baseline: the p95 < 120ms target is measured from a customer backend inside the same region via private peering (so Frankfurt->Frankfurt; Tokyo->Tokyo). If you measure from a browser in a different region, add network transit times — we can include an explicit measurement method in the SLA matrix. See attached SLA_throughput_matrix.xlsx for measurement points and test harness.

- Failover: our routing policy supports automatic failover to alternate pools (US primary -> EU/APAC as configured). App-level retries remain recommended for in-flight request resilience. To minimize latency spike during failover we do:
  * warm-standby cache (KV prefix warming)
  * session affinity fallback (we continue to honor session tokens within the warm standby if present)
  * pre-provisioned cross-region bandwidth and priority queuing for cutover windows
Estimated RTO: 60–120s depending on session size and cache hit rate. We'll include runbook steps in the SOW.

- Term/pricing: attached pricing_sheet_q1_2026.xlsx includes three options: 24-month standard, 12-month higher-commit, and a stepped-commit 12->24 plan. We'll walk through during the sync.

Attaching: network_diagram.png, SLA_throughput_matrix.xlsx

See you Monday 09:00 CET. Meeting invite incoming from Aditya.

— Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@omnihealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated capacity expansion & term amendment — OmniHealth (legal redlines)

Liam / Aditya — Priya from Legal. We reviewed the draft amendment and have a few redlines to standardize for enterprise procurement: 

1) Data residency/data access: we will explicitly state that customer PII stored in EU pool remains in EU and access controls/audit logs must be scoped to EU region unless otherwise authorized.
2) Indemnity: propose limiting carveouts to gross negligence/willful misconduct; request OmniHealth review on your side for parity.
3) Termination for convenience: propose 90-day notice for early termination of the incremental capacity, with pro-rata refund of unused prepaid amounts.

I've attached Amendment_redlines_20260222.pdf with inline comments. Once we sync and agree commercial terms, we can circulate a DocuSign-ready packet. If OmniHealth has in-house counsel, happy to coordinate a 30-minute call to speed redline resolution.

— Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated capacity expansion & term amendment — OmniHealth (next steps & DocuSign)

Liam / Sofia — thanks for the productive sync today. Recap and confirmed next steps: 

Recap
- OmniHealth to commit to regional pools: EU 24 GPUs, APAC 24 GPUs; US pool unchanged for now.
- SLOs: p95 latency measured from regional private peer, p95 < 120ms for <=512 tokens; failover RTO target 90s (documented in SOW).
- Commercial path: OmniHealth to choose between 24-month standard or 12-month higher-commit. Pricing options were left on the table — see pricing_sheet_q1_2026.xlsx.
- Legal: Priya shared redlines; OmniHealth counsel can propose parity edits.

Action items
1) Aditya: circulate DocuSign amendment with the negotiated options for selection — link below.
2) Monica / Karthik: set up peering checklist and STAGING provisioning timeline (target: staging provision Apr 5, prod cutover Apr 15).
3) Liam: confirm preferred contract term option and share any internal PO timelines by end of week.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/omn/record/7291
